# Online Shopping System Advanced — starter kit

Unpack this into the repository you are going to build in. It is the harness the specification assumes exists, with every file already at its real path.

## Do these five things first

| # | Do | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Fill in the build, test and lint commands in [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) | They are the definition of done that everything else refers to. Until they are real, `make verify` is a placeholder. |
| 2 | Run `make verify` and make it pass on an empty project | A verification command that has never passed is not a gate. |
| 3 | Commit all of this, before writing any application code | It is the point you come back to, and the first thing a reviewer will look for. |
| 4 | Read `CLAUDE.md` yourself, once | It is what an agent reads instead of asking you. Anything wrong in it is wrong in everything it produces. |
| 5 | Run `/build-slice` | It reads the specification, proposes the slice list, and builds the first one. This is where code starts. |

## What is in here

| File | What it does |
|---|---|
| [`.claude/agents/reviewer.md`](.claude/agents/reviewer.md) | A reviewer that runs on a different session from the author, pointed at `REVIEW.md`. |
| [`.claude/settings.json`](.claude/settings.json) | Hooks. Includes the one that stops a test being edited to make a failing check pass — that is not a matter of trust, it is a boundary. |
| [`.github/workflows/review.yml`](.github/workflows/review.yml) | The same review in CI, so it happens whether or not somebody remembers. |
| [`.github/workflows/scan.yml`](.github/workflows/scan.yml) | A recurring scan, for the checks that only matter on a schedule. |
| [`AGENTS.md`](AGENTS.md) | The cross-tool name for the same thing. One line pointing at `CLAUDE.md`, so there is one authority rather than two that drift. |
| [`BUILD-LOG.md`](BUILD-LOG.md) | One entry per slice. The handover between sessions. |
| [`CLAUDE.md`](CLAUDE.md) | The context file. Build commands with their healthy output, the conventions, and the mistakes agents keep making here. The highest-return file in the repository. |
| [`Makefile`](Makefile) | `make verify` — the one command that decides whether a change is correct. State it as the definition of done. |
| [`autonomy-policy.yaml`](autonomy-policy.yaml) | What an agent may do, per environment, and the actions no agent may take anywhere. A change to this file is a reviewable change, which is the point. |

## Capabilities in this specification

`administration`, `audit-trail`, `authentication`, `payments`, `authorisation`, `search`, `authentication-sessions`, `authentication-signup`

Build them one at a time, as vertical slices, in dependency order. Each has its own folder in both halves of the specification.

## One thing that is not a file

**Incident becomes a test.** Closes the outer loop. The step that decides whether the method compounds or just spins.

```bash
# An incident does not close until this exists — control UT-AI-11.
#
# 1. Reproduce the failure as a test that fails on the current code.
# 2. Fix the code, not the test.
# 3. Add the case to the evaluation suite if an agent was involved.
# 4. Name the test in the incident record.

claude -p "Read incident-record.md. Write a failing regression test that reproduces \
  INC-042 and cites the requirement it breaches. Do not fix the code yet." \
  --allowedTools "Read,Grep,Glob,Write,Bash(pytest:*)"

pytest -q tests/regression/test_inc_042.py   # must FAIL first
# then fix the code, and it must pass
```
